messages.author: 05954d53fb9c89d2
messages.subject: Models with an analytic solution
parts:
Hi all,
I have a general question about models with an analytic solution.
For models with an analytic solution, does STAN compute the posterior estimates analytically or still use MCMC?
May I be less worried about the convergence of these models?


Thank you very much!
Jing

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Models with an analytic solution
parts:
On Monday, March 27, 2017 at 9:25:26 AM UTC-4, Jing Dong wrote:
For models with an analytic solution, does STAN compute the posterior estimates analytically or still use MCMC?
MCMC. The Stan language has almost no logic capabilities and cannot infer when there is an analytical solution.
May I be less worried about the convergence of these models?

No, but convergence is rarely a problem for Stan. Mixing can be a problem but if the model is simple enough to have an analytical solution, then NUTS will probably mix really quickly.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Models with an analytic solution
parts:
No, Stan doesn't exploit any conjugacy---it just does HMC
on the log density.

If you have analytic posteriors, you don't need to use Stan!

Or if you can't do pure Monte Carlo on the analytic posterior,
just code up the posterior in Stan directly---the log density only
has to be equal to the posterior up to a constant---it doesn't have to
be the log joint. There's a section in the optimization chapter
of the manual on how to do this for (partial) analytic posteriors.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Models with an analytic solution
parts:
Two things we could do to speed things up:

1. Recognize conjugacy and marginalize out intermediate
parameters. Sufficient statistics can also be calculated
in a lot of cases. I don't see how to make this automatic,
but there's a lot we could provide in the way of built-in
special functions that could be used to speedup particular
models without much work.

2. Provide built-in functions for common models with
analytic gradients---I got a 3.5 x speedup for logistic
regression doing this, so we're going to want to roll out
all the basic GLMs this way.

- Bob
